note: INSTRUMENT (Step 3b): confirmed SAS-SV. The paper: 'We used SAS-SV, which was developed by Kwon et al. [35] ... ten items ... six-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree, 2 = disagree, 3 = weakly disagree, 4 = weakly agree, 5 = agree, and 6 = strongly agree)'; live data 10 items sas1..sas10 on 1..6, deposit sas_sc range 10-60 -- matches the SAS-SV, not the PHQ-9/PSS-4/ISI in the same file. MAPPING (paper_order, in the sense of the instrument's printed numbering): the S1 xlsx is one sheet with bare headers sas1..sas10, numeric 1-6 cells, no comments, codebook or labels; the paper prints no item. data/roy_2024_fgid_screeners.py melts the columns by name, so the IRW code IS the source column name; what is inferred is that column sasN is SAS-SV item N as numbered in Kwon's Appendix S1 / Table 3. Tested in verify_roy_2024_sas_sv.R (VERDICT: PASS, 1,019 respondents): live per-item x level counts equal the deposit in 60/60 cells; block structure: each of items 1-3 (daily-life disturbance: missed work, concentration, wrist/neck pain) correlates more with its own block than with items 4-7 (withdrawal) and vice versa, 7/7 (own vs other mean r: sas1 .435/.289, sas2 .450/.292, sas3 .314/.304 -- thin, sas4 .477/.351, sas5 .510/.290, sas6 .451/.312, sas7 .427/.226). Not established: order within each block, or the positions of sas8, sas9, sas10 -- hence PARTIAL. Descriptive only: Spearman +0.71 between live item means and Kwon's Table 3 means (Korean adolescents; different population). OPTIONS: Kwon's Appendix S1 prints Strongly disagree / Disagree / Weakly disagree / Weakly agree / Agree / Strongly agree over 1..6, and the Roy paper states the same labels and numbers. Direction corroborated: deposit sas_sc equals the raw row sum of sas1..10 for 1019/1019 rows, and sas_sc correlates +0.265 with phq_sc, +0.299 with isi_sc, +0.204 with pss_sc (a reversed coding would flip all three). TEXT: item_text transcribed verbatim from Kwon's Appendix S1 cells, including the curly apostrophe in item 4 ('Won’t') and the terminal periods on items 7 and 10 only; leading item numbers are separate cells and not shipped. Kwon's appendix carries no instruction sentence and the Roy paper prints none, so instructions is blank rather than reconstructed. Instrument name is the paper's and Kwon's 'Smartphone Addiction Scale - Short Version (SAS-SV)' (ASCII hyphen). LANGUAGE: the paper does NOT state the administration language, and for the SAS-SV it cites only Kwon et al. (whose English version ships here). language=Bengali follows the sibling roy_2024_phq9 (batch_451), which inferred a Bengali Google Form from the paper's citation of a Bengali PHQ adaptation (ref 34, PMID 15887819); the SAS-SV sits on that same form. That inference is weaker here, since no Bengali SAS-SV is cited, and an English administration cannot be excluded. No Bengali wording in scope: the S1 xlsx has no Bengali-script text (all string codes English) and the article XML has none; the Google Form was not deposited. So the fallback applies: the developers' official English in the base fields, no _translated columns, language=Bengali, which keeps the table findable by the backfill query. RIGHTS: no instrument_rights_register row for the SAS-SV (the Zung-SAS row explicitly notes the name collision and does not cover this instrument). The originator's own publication, Kwon et al. 2013 PLoS ONE, is CC BY 4.0 and prints the English items and anchors in its Appendix S1; no fee, permission-required, NC, ND or no-redistribution clause from the holder was found. Third-party validation papers report having obtained author permission to translate/use it -- a practice they describe, not a clause the holder states -- so silence is permission and nothing blocks. Precedent: mhscdc_fried_2020_smartphone (batch_202) shipped SAS-SV wording from the same Kwon source. No register row written (a round may not write ship). SOURCE-INTERNAL DISCREPANCY (not an item-text defect, not a mapping issue): the deposit's sas_cat does not follow the cut-offs the paper's Methods state (not addicted <31 male / <33 female, high risk 31-39 / 33-39, addicted >=40). It classifies sas_sc <=21 as Not addicted, 22-31 (male) / 22-33 (female) as High risk, and 32+ (male) / 34+ (female) as Addicted; applying the stated cut-offs agrees with sas_cat for only 580/1019 rows. The paper's Table 1 (35 / 148 / 836) reports the deposit's categories, so its 82.04% 'Addicted' figure rests on the lower thresholds. Sample mean sas_sc 39.19 (SD 8.51) against Kwon's 25.26 in adolescents.
public_note: The paper does not state the administration language; the questionnaire was probably administered in Bengali, but no Bengali wording is published in this study's deposit, so the item and option text shipped here is the scale developers' official English (Kwon et al. 2013, Appendix S1) rather than necessarily the sentences respondents read.
